title: Context Management and Anti-Bloat (Three Compilers)
description: Scoping compilation, progress compilation, and retry handoff — do not let the working agent keep its own notes
detail:
CHYing-agent (Top 9 in a past authorized assessment exercise) lessons:
1. PromptCompiler: before working a target, use a lightweight model to compile reconnaissance data and the target description into a structured summary (attack-surface layers, priority directions, key constraints) — scope the work before acting
2. ProgressCompiler: when context is nearly full, an independent lightweight agent reads all progress files and generates a concise handoff brief. Lesson learned: letting the working agent keep its own notes inevitably causes uncontrolled bloat (context overflow → note-taking → note bloat → reading notes causes overflow again)
3. RetryHandoffCompiler: when revisiting an old target, compile the historical attack chain into a continuation report and resume from the stall point instead of re-exploring
Sapper's corresponding approach: facts are the blackboard (record only incremental facts), the doc layer holds evidence details and is not injected into prompts by default, and recall fetches on demand — naturally resistant to bloat.
Source: https://github.com/yhy0/CHYing-agent
